newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TAYLOR FIT FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR FIT FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: Australian captain Mark Taylor has recovered from a back injury and will be fit to lead his team in the second test against South Africa beginning in Port Elizabeth on Friday.
"He has had no adverse reaction after a full net and fielding practice this morning and will definitely play on Friday," coach Geoff Marsh told reporters on Wednesday.

Taylor has been suffering from the injury (muscle spasms and pain in lower right side of the back) since last Friday morning when he was forced to pull out of Australia's three-day match against Border in East London.
He has been severely limited in his movements since then.
"He's basically been swimming, stretching and lying flat on his back for the last three or four days, which may explain why he felt a bit light-headed after the practice. But he is fine," Marsh said.
Taylor underwent surgery on his back last year and was ruled out of the game for two months. But the latest problem is thought to be unrelated to his previous injury.
Australia hope to clinch the three-test series in Port Elizabeth after winning the first test in Johannesburg last week by an innings and 196 runs.
